[Rating: 1/10] Zero effort to design. Pyramid solitaire already exists in a much better form than this.

[Rating: 3/10] 2024-12-17  Initial Rating: 6.0 (December 2024)  • I love communication-limited games, so my desire to play Ultimatch was high. Sadly, the game didn’t live up to the expectation. It is too simple, and the communication limits don’t work well here.  • The game is pure abstract—there is no theme whatsoever. You’re just playing with colors and patterns, which is fine.  • Gameplay is very straightforward. Players work as a team to match symbols or colors in a pyramid structure. [Rating: 3/10] Filler game but even at that level, there's not much of a game. There are minimal decision making in the game and the barebones "strategy" is to setup situations that let you draw more cards. Even then, there's not any meaningful decisions there either.

[Rating: 4/10] Maybe fine for a midnight closer? We didn't find this challenging at all and easily won the game and never came close to losing.

[Rating: 4/10] The box says it supports 5 players, but that is a lie.  At 5 players, players can only make 1 Ultimatch before the deck runs out and all remaining cards are in players' hands or in the alta-hand.  I still enjoy the concept of Ultimatch and would like to try it with 2 players, but never again with 5.
